Restarting doesn't delete your data." } ] }, { id: 'exercise', title: 'How do I track my exercise and activities with Fitbit?', short: 'Exercise', category: 'Exercise & activity', tags: ['data', 'exercise', 'activity', 'workout', 'run', 'running', 'log'], excerpt: 'There are several ways to ensure that your workouts or other calorie-burning activities are calculated in your daily totals.', sections: [ { h: 'Multisport and exercise modes', p: 'Some trackers let you start an exercise from the tracker itself, so you can see real-time stats while you work out.' }, { h: 'SmartTrack', p: 'SmartTrack automatically recognizes many continuous activities, such as walks and runs, and records them in your exercise history.' }, { h: 'MobileRun', p: 'Use your phone’s GPS in the Fitbit app to record a run, walk or hike with distance, pace and a map of your route.' }, { h: 'Manually logging an exercise', p: 'If your tracker didn’t record a run, add it yourself: in the Fitbit app, tap the + icon, choose Track exercise, then Log previous exercise and enter the time and distance.' }, { h: 'FitStar', p: 'Guided video workouts in the app add their sessions to your exercise history automatically.' } ] }, { id: 'syncing', title: "Why won't my tracker sync?", short: 'Syncing', category: 'Syncing', tags: ['syncing', 'sync', 'data', 'mobile app', 'bluetooth'], excerpt: 'Syncing difficulty is usually caused by a missing requirement. Verify each one before moving on to the troubleshooting steps.', sections: [ { h: 'Requirements', p: 'The Bluetooth setting on your phone or computer must be on, the Fitbit app must be up to date, and your tracker needs some battery charge. On Android, location permission must be on for Bluetooth scanning.' }, { h: 'Sync manually', p: 'Open the Fitbit app, pull down on the dashboard and wait for the sync to finish. Keep your tracker close to your phone while it syncs.' }, { h: 'Restart Bluetooth and the app', p: 'Turn Bluetooth off and on again, force-quit the Fitbit app and reopen it. If it still won’t sync, restart your phone and your tracker.' }, { h: 'Remove other connections', p: 'Your tracker can only sync with one device at a time. Close the Fitbit app on other phones or tablets nearby.' } ] }, { id: 'howsync', title: 'How do Fitbit trackers sync their data?', short: 'How syncing works', category: 'Syncing', tags: ['sync', 'syncing', 'data', 'bluetooth'], excerpt: 'Your tracker sends its data to the Fitbit app over Bluetooth, and the app sends it to your Fitbit account.', sections: [ { h: 'Syncing with your phone', p: 'When the Fitbit app is open, or all-day sync is on, your tracker syncs over Bluetooth whenever it’s nearby.' }, { h: 'Syncing with a computer', p: 'On a Windows 10 computer, the Fitbit app syncs over Bluetooth. Older computers can use Fitbit Connect with a wireless sync dongle.' }, { h: 'How often should I sync?', p: 'Your tracker stores about a week of detailed data. Sync at least once every few days so nothing is lost.' } ] }, { id: 'lights', title: 'What do the light patterns mean on my Flex 2?', short: 'Light patterns', category: 'Getting to know your tracker', tags: ['lights', 'light patterns', 'flex 2', 'flex', 'led', 'goal'], excerpt: 'Flex 2 has five indicator lights. Their patterns show your progress toward your daily goal, battery level and notifications.', sections: [ { h: 'Light pattern summary', p: 'Double-tap your tracker to see your progress. Each light is 20% of your daily goal, and a blinking light shows the 20% you’re working on now.', lights: true }, { h: 'Reaching your goal', p: 'When you reach your daily goal, your tracker vibrates and the lights flash in a celebration pattern.' }, { h: 'Battery level', p: 'While charging, the lights show the battery level. Each solid light is about 20% charged; when all five are solid, your tracker is full.' }, { h: 'Notifications', p: 'When a call, text or calendar alert arrives, your tracker vibrates and the lights flash in the color set for that notification.' }, { h: 'Reminders to move', p: 'If you haven’t moved in a while, your tracker vibrates and the lights sweep across to remind you to get up.' } ] }, { id: 'notifications', title: 'How do I get call and text notifications?', short: 'Notifications', category: 'Notifications', tags: ['notifications', 'notification', 'calls', 'call', 'texts'], excerpt: 'Supported trackers buzz and light up when your phone gets a call, text or calendar alert, so you don’t miss one.', sections: [ { h: 'Turn on notifications', p: 'In the Fitbit app, tap your tracker, then Notifications. Turn on Calls, Text messages or Calendar events.' }, { h: 'Choose a light color', p: 'Flex 2 can flash a different color for each kind of notification, so you know a call from a text without looking at your phone.' }, { h: 'Not getting notifications?', p: 'Keep your phone within about 30 feet, make sure Do Not Disturb is off, and keep the Fitbit app running in the background.' } ] }, { id: 'hr', title: 'What should I know about my heart-rate data?', short: 'Heart rate', category: 'Heart rate', tags: ['data', 'heart rate', 'hr', 'cardio'], excerpt: 'Trackers with heart-rate sensors estimate your heart rate all day. Fit and placement affect accuracy the most.', sections: [ { h: 'How heart rate is measured', p: 'Green lights on the back of the tracker measure changes in blood volume in your wrist, which the tracker turns into beats per minute.' }, { h: 'Getting the most accurate reading', p: 'Wear the tracker a finger’s width above your wrist bone. During exercise, wear it a little higher and snugger.' }, { h: 'What is my cardio fitness score?', p: 'Your cardio fitness score estimates your VO2 max from your resting heart rate, your profile and, when available, your runs with GPS.' } ] }, { id: 'sleep', title: 'How do I track my sleep?', short: 'Sleep', category: 'Sleep', tags: ['data', 'sleep'], excerpt: 'Wear your tracker to bed and it records sleep automatically. Sleep stages need a tracker with heart rate.', sections: [ { h: 'Automatic sleep tracking', p: 'Your tracker notices when you’ve been still for about an hour and records it as sleep. Sync in the morning to see the results.' }, { h: 'What should I know about sleep stages?', p: 'Trackers with heart-rate sensors estimate light, deep and REM sleep using movement and heart-rate patterns.' }, { h: 'Why does my sleep look wrong?', p: 'Wear the tracker snugly on your non-dominant wrist and check that its sleep sensitivity setting is Normal.' } ] }, { id: 'calories', title: 'How does Fitbit estimate how many calories I burn?', short: 'Calories', category: 'Food & calories', tags: ['data', 'calories', 'activity'], excerpt: 'Calorie estimates combine your basal metabolic rate with your activity data. Keeping your profile up to date makes them more accurate.', sections: [ { h: 'Basal metabolic rate', p: 'Your BMR is the calories your body burns at rest, estimated from your height, weight, sex and age. It counts even while you sleep.' }, { h: 'Activity', p: 'Steps, active minutes and heart rate (when available) add to your BMR to give your total for the day.' }, { h: 'What are active minutes?', p: 'Active minutes count time spent in moderate-to-vigorous activity, in bouts of ten minutes or more.' } ] }, { id: 'setup', title: 'How do I set up my Fitbit device?', short: 'Setting up', category: 'Getting started', tags: ['setting up', 'setup', 'set up', 'app', 'pair', 'new'], excerpt: 'Set up your tracker with the Fitbit app on your phone, tablet or computer. Check the compatibility list for your exact phone.' } ] }, { id: 'firmware', title: "How do I update my tracker's firmware?", short: 'Firmware update', category: 'Troubleshooting', tags: ['firmware update', 'firmware', 'update'], excerpt: 'Updates bring new features and fixes. Keep your phone close to your tracker until it finishes.' }, { h: 'If the update gets stuck', p: 'Restart your phone and your tracker, make sure the battery is above 50%, and try again.' } ] }, { id: 'damaged', title: 'What should I do if my tracker is damaged?', short: 'Damaged', category: 'Troubleshooting', tags: ['damaged', 'broken', 'warranty', 'returns'], excerpt: 'Check your warranty status first.
